title: Check for a palindrome
description: Write a function `is_palindrome(text)` that returns True if `text`, compared case-insensitively, reads the same forwards and backwards. Spaces are not stripped or ignored, only the letter case is normalized.
hints: You need to compare the text to its own reverse, but case should not matter.
`str.lower()` normalizes case, and slicing with a step of -1 reverses a string.
Lower-case `text` first with `.lower()`, then compare that result to itself reversed using `[::-1]`, and return whether they are equal.
expected_behavior: Returns True if the lower-cased text equals its own reverse, and False otherwise.
explanation: `text.lower()` normalizes the case so that 'Racecar' and 'racecar' are treated the same. Slicing with `[::-1]` produces the reversed string without a loop, and comparing the lowered text to its reverse tells us whether it reads the same both ways.
